surfaces.part: water terrain tile fill (dark teal, uniform 16x16 with small highlights)

answer.evidence: The tile is a full 16x16 block of dark teal water/ground texture with scattered lighter pixels (a few teal highlight marks near rows 0-2 and a light dot near row 13). Every column scan shows one continuous run over rows 0-15 with near-constant lightness, and the width is 16 on every row. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical face. It is a flat terrain fill with no standing structure, so it reads as a top-down slab, which is expected for a terrain tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small dark teal patch with only a few light specks. The measured 51% near-flat coverage is far above both references (0%), so about half the surface is flat fill. It has 5 raw colours, against 26 per tile for the grass reference, and I see only about 3 usable shading steps. The grass reference has clustered blade tufts in several greens and the paving has stone-by-stone shading. The candidate has no tufts, grain or per-element shading, only a flat base with a couple of highlight dots. Its dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so it is not a black-outline sticker, and its 5 visible tones per tile do edge past the grass reference's 3. But the flat fill and the lack of visible texture make it clearly flatter and poorer than the Beodeul grass and paving.
